chunks: Sa'd ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and 'Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prays the voluntary prayer while he is on a beast of burden in the cities, he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: Cities or urban areas (plural of masrah)
key_terms.دَابَّةٍ: Beast of burden (animal used for riding)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray voluntary prayers while riding a horse or camel in the city?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayers regarding the necessity of dismounting, ruling that riding an animal is permissible for nafl even within city limits (al-amSar). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that while dismounting is preferred or required for fard prayers in settled areas to show reverence, the flexibility of nafl allows for ease during travel or daily movement. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of key figures like Ibn Abi Umayr and Hammad ibn Uthman in the Tusi's Tahdhib.
